post.summary: Ask OpenVibe.Chat for the sound of one line, in the person own voice and on the person allowance (the Agent Streams plan, S4).
post.description: **chat.tts.speak** (first-party): Ask OpenVibe.Chat for the sound of one line, in the person own voice and on the person allowance (the Agent Streams plan, S4). The caller presents a service token for audience openvibe.chat that names the person it acts for (a node token on_behalf_of), so the voice is that person and never another. The text is one line (220 characters at most). The answer is the audio (base64) with its type; the desk mixes it into the stream Opus track. A person own cloned voice is asked for by name and only by that person.

get.description: **chat.inbox.read** (public): Read the support inboxes the person works in on OpenVibe.Chat (docs/platform.md): the inboxes, each one's conversations (waiting first) and messages, and its saved replies; the owner also exports every conversation (JSON or CSV). Visitors' messages are people's words to a team, so an app sees only inboxes its person works in, and the person's own role decides the rest (the export is the owner's).

GET /internal/chat/rooms/agent:digest?since= answers chat.agent-digest@1: at most ten items and 1,500 characters, each with who (the display name and the handle), what (cut to 200 characters), its kind (a question, a suggestion or a reaction) and its upvotes. chat.agent-digest.v1.title: ChatAgentDigest
chat.agent-digest.v1.description: chat.agent-digest@1 (the Agent Streams plan, S5): what a chat room said to an agent between two of its steps, GET /api/v1/rooms/agent:<id>/digest?since= on OpenVibe.Chat. The agent never reads the raw room: it asks for a digest and gets at most ten items and 1,500 characters. Each item names who (the display name and the handle), what (cut to 200 characters), its kind (a question, a suggestion or a reaction) and its upvotes (a thumbs up on the message counts). Chat chooses what goes in: repeats are grouped, greetings and spam are dropped, and the most-upvoted questions and suggestions come first. Nobody is left out by accident: a person who is timed out or banned, whose account is younger than a day, or who set 'Agents don't read my messages' is never in the digest. A link is kept as its domain only ('a link to github.com'), because the agent never follows a link from chat. The code and the commands stay as text: the agent's own tools and approvals decide what may run, never chat.

room.description: The room the digest came from: an agent stream's room, `agent:<ags_id>`.

since.description: The start of the window: the moment the agent last read, or null for the first read.

until.description: The end of the window: the moment this digest was made.

items.description: What chat said, at most ten items. The order is the one Chat chose: the most-upvoted questions and suggestions first, the reactions last.

who.description: Who said it: the display name and the handle. Never an id, never an email, never anything else about them.

handle.description: The handle, so the agent can answer this person by name.

what.description: What they said, cut to 200 characters. A link is kept as its domain only.

kind.description: What the line is: a question the agent may answer, a suggestion it may take or leave, or a reaction (a thumbs up, a cheer) that says nothing to do.

upvotes.description: How many thumbs up the message carries. The most-upvoted items come first.

repeated.description: How many people said this same thing. Chat groups repeats into one item; this is the number behind it.

chars.description: How many characters the items use together, at most 1,500.

truncated.description: True when Chat left something out because of the ten-item or 1,500-character cap.

chat.agent-poll.v1.title: ChatAgentPoll
chat.agent-poll.v1.description: chat.agent-poll@1 (the Agent Streams plan, S5): a poll the agent asks a Co-pilot room to run, and the result it gets back. The agent writes the question and two to four options ('Which name: parseRows or readTable?') and the poll is open for 30 to 120 seconds. Chat draws it as a poll card with buttons; `!1` to `!4` vote too. One vote per person, one poll at a time, and at most one poll every five minutes. The owner (or a moderator) can close a poll early or veto its result. A poll can only choose between the options the agent wrote: Chat never adds one. The result carries the counts, nothing else about who voted.

room.description: The room the poll is in: an agent stream's room, `agent:<ags_id>`.

options.description: The options the agent wrote, two to four of them. Chat never adds an option of its own.

id.description: The option's number: `!1` to `!4` vote for it.

label.description: The option's text, as the agent wrote it.

votes.description: How many people chose it. The count is in the result; it says nothing about who.

closes_at.description: When the poll closes on its own: 30 to 120 seconds after it opened.

closed_at.description: When the poll was closed early by the owner or a moderator, or null when it ran its time.

state.description: Where the poll stands: open, closed (the counts are final), or vetoed (the owner or a moderator refused the result).

result.description: The result, once the poll is closed: the counts and the winning option. Null while the poll is open.

counts.description: How many votes each option got, in the order the options were written.

winner.description: The option that won, or null when there was no vote or no winner.

vetoed_by.description: Who vetoed the result (the owner or a moderator), or null. Never a person's id: the handle only.

chat.channel-moderation-result.v1.title: ChatChannelModerationResult
chat.channel-moderation-result.v1.description: chat.channel-moderation-result@1: the answer of GET /internal/moderation/channels/:channelId on OpenVibe.Chat (capability chat.moderation.read): { ok: true, settings, moderator_ids } — one channel's moderation settings and the ids of the people who moderate it, for OpenVibe.Live's stream chat. settings carries every channel_moderation_settings column (Live's own defaults when the channel has no row yet, database.js getChannelModerationSettings); the switches are 0/1 as the table stores them. moderator_ids are Live user ids (channel_moderators.user_id), never names. A failure is { ok: false, error }; a caller without the grant gets 401 { ok: false }.

moderator_ids.description: The channel's moderators, oldest first (channel_moderators.created_at); empty when it has none.

flag.description: A switch as the SQLite table stores it.

settings.description: One row of channel_moderation_settings, or Live's defaults for a channel that has no row. Every column is present; the switches are 0/1.

caps_percentage_limit.description: Percent of a message that may be capitals; 0 means off.

slur_filter_terms.description: Extra terms, comma separated; a channel's own filter list, never a network-wide secret.

slur_filter_disabled_categories.description: A JSON array string of disabled built-in categories ('[]' when none).

ip_approval_mode.description: 0 off, 1 approve before chatting, 2 approved addresses only.

soundboard_banned_ids.description: Banned channel sound ids, comma separated.

emote_scale.description: Emote display size in chat, percent of the base height (100 is the default).

donation_sound_url.description: Optional alert sounds set by the streamer; absent or null when unset.

updated_at.description: When the row was last written; absent or null when the channel still has its defaults.

chat.dm-peers-result.v1.title: ChatDmPeersResult
chat.dm-peers-result.v1.description: chat.dm-peers-result@1: which of the candidate people share a conversation with one person on OpenVibe.Chat (POST /internal/chat/dm/peers, chat.dm.peers.read). It answers with subjects only; a candidate with no shared conversation is simply absent. Used by OpenVibe.Network's presence privacy rule.

subject.description: The person whose conversations were read.

peers.description: The candidates that share at least one conversation with them, as subjects.

chat.event-request.v1.title: ChatEventRequest
chat.event-request.v1.description: chat.event-request@1: what a first-party service hands OpenVibe.Chat's POST /internal/chat/events (chat.event.publish) to push a transient frame to chat sockets: cards, alerts, sounds, media queue state, call invites. Nothing is stored; Chat broadcasts the frame to the target. Applied once per (caller, key): a retry with the same key and body answers the first result, the same key with another body gets 409. Chat also refuses a frame whose JSON is longer than 16384 characters or that has a __proto__, constructor or prototype key; a news card's timestamp must parse as a date.

key.description: Idempotency key, scoped to the caller and to this route.

kind.description: stream: one stream's room; channel: a channel owner's room; owner-streams: every stream of that owner; global: the homepage global chat; all: every socket; user: one person's sockets (call frames only).

id.description: The stream, channel owner or user id; required for stream, channel, owner-streams and user, absent or null for global and all.

type.description: The client frame type. chat is only the transient news card (never saved); a stored line goes through chat.message.send.

streamerId.description: The channel owner; must equal target.id with target.kind channel.

streamId.description: Must equal target.id with target.kind stream.

chat.inbox-conversations-result.v1.title: ChatInboxConversationsResult
chat.inbox-conversations-result.v1.description: chat.inbox-conversations-result@1: an inbox's conversations ({ conversations }: waiting first, each with status, who has it, the visitor's name and whether their site verified them, a preview and unread count), one conversation's messages ({ conversation, messages }, ?after= a message id), a reply ({ message }), its saved replies ({ replies }), or the owner's export (?format=json: { inbox, exported_at, conversations: [{ …, messages }] }; ?format=csv is text/csv, one row per message). A message is { id, author: visitor | agent | ai | system, author_name, body, created_at, account? }.

chat.inbox-reply-request.v1.title: ChatInboxReplyRequest
chat.inbox-reply-request.v1.description: chat.inbox-reply-request@1: what one of an inbox's people sends while working a conversation (chat.inbox.reply). A reply (POST /api/chat/inboxes/:id/conversations/:cid/messages { message }: the conversation becomes open, Vibe stays quiet in it, and the person takes it if nobody has); a status or an assignment (PATCH /:id/conversations/:cid { status: open | resolved | bot, assignee_id: one of the inbox's people | null }); a translation (POST /:id/conversations/:cid/messages/:mid/translate { to } or POST /:id/translate { text, to }). Marking read (POST /:id/conversations/:cid/read) takes no body.

chat.inbox-request.v1.title: ChatInboxRequest
chat.inbox-request.v1.description: chat.inbox-request@1: a support inbox, made (POST /api/chat/inboxes, name required) or changed by its owner (PATCH /api/chat/inboxes/:id, any subset). Unknown fields are ignored; a bad value is 422 with a code (inbox.name, inbox.origin, inbox.hours, inbox.retention, …). Members (POST /:id/members { username }), saved replies (POST /:id/replies { shortcut, body }), webhooks (POST /:id/webhooks { url }), actions (POST /:id/actions { name, description, url, params }) and verified visitors (POST /:id/identity { action: on | rotate | off }) take their own small bodies on the routes chat.inbox.manage names.

greeting.description: The first line a visitor sees.

ai_instructions.description: What Vibe should know and how to answer (content, never rules that override Chat's).

knowledge_urls.description: https pages Vibe may read (an array, or one a line).

allowed_origins.description: The sites the widget answers (empty: any).

handoff.description: The inbox's people answer too (false: a site assistant where only Vibe answers).

hours.description: When the people answer; null: always.

route.description: round_robin: a visitor waiting for a person goes to the next of the people.

retention_days.description: How long finished conversations stay; null: forever.

chat.inbox-result.v1.title: ChatInboxResult
chat.inbox-result.v1.description: chat.inbox-result@1: a support inbox as its people see it ({ inbox, members?, embed? }: the widget snippet and panel address), or the inboxes a person works in ({ inboxes }, each with their role and how many conversations wait and are open). Secrets (the identity secret, webhook and action secrets) appear only on the answer that made them.

chat.ingress-ack.v1.title: ChatIngressAck
chat.ingress-ack.v1.description: chat.ingress-ack@1: what OpenVibe.Chat's service ingress answers when there is nothing to return (POST /internal/chat/events, chat.event.publish; POST /internal/chat/invalidate, chat.cache.invalidate), and the error every /internal/chat route answers: 400 a body Chat refuses, 401/403 no service token or no grant for the capability, 403/404 a refused or unknown DM participant or stream, 409 an idempotency key reused with another body, 503 Chat unavailable or a delivery in progress (retry with the same key).

chat.invalidate-request.v1.title: ChatInvalidateRequest
chat.invalidate-request.v1.description: chat.invalidate-request@1: what a first-party service hands OpenVibe.Chat's POST /internal/chat/invalidate (chat.cache.invalidate) after it changed something Chat caches (a person, a channel, IP approvals, bans). A cache hint only: Chat drops and reloads the entry (with user_data, it also pushes the person's new name and look to their sockets). At least one hint is required. Applied once per (caller, key).

key.description: Idempotency key, scoped to the caller and to this route.

user.description: A person whose cached row is stale.

user_data.description: The person's new public fields, pushed to their sockets; id must equal user.

approvals.description: A channel whose IP approvals changed.

channel.description: A channel whose cached settings changed.

chat.messages-page.v1.title: ChatMessagesPage
chat.messages-page.v1.description: chat.messages-page@1: the answer of GET /internal/chat/messages on OpenVibe.Chat (capability chat.messages.read), which pages non-deleted chat_messages for OpenVibe.Live's AI context, clip and viewer jobs and its moderator search and history. Query: one filter of channel_user_id, stream_id, user_id, anon_id, username or id (one message), a cursor on id (after_id ascending, before_id descending), limit, and tail=1 (no rows, only max_id). max_id is the highest id matching the filter, null when none, so a caller can resume after it. A failure is chat.ingress-ack@1's error.

message.description: One chat_messages row (Chat's columns, as stored).

user_id.description: Live user id; null for an anonymous or relayed sender.

channel_user_id.description: The broadcaster whose channel room it is.

source_platform.description: The relay platform of a relayed line; null for OpenVibe chat.

timestamp.description: UTC 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', as Chat stores it (ov_now()).

chat.moderation-queue-result.v1.title: ChatModerationQueueResult
chat.moderation-queue-result.v1.description: chat.moderation-queue-result@1: what OpenVibe.Chat's moderation queue reads answer (capability chat.moderation.queue.read), one shape per route, for OpenVibe.Live's moderator pages: GET /internal/chat/moderation/pending-ip?channel_id → { pending_ip } (a channel's messages held for IP approval, status pending, oldest first); GET /internal/chat/moderation/relay-users?channel_id → { relay_users } (relay names hidden or banned on the channel or everywhere, newest first); GET /internal/chat/moderation/relay-users/:id → { relay_user } (one, null when unknown); GET /internal/chat/moderation/tts-override?identity_key → { tts_override } (null when none). Internal: rows carry IP addresses. A failure is chat.ingress-ack@1's error.

ip_address.description: The sender's address: internal, never shown outside moderation.

created_at.description: UTC 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', as Chat stores it.

channel_id.description: null hides the name on every channel.

created_by_username.description: The moderator's name from Chat's copy of the user, when known.

created_at.description: UTC 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', as Chat stores it.

identity_key.description: Lowercased identity the override applies to.

updated_at.description: UTC 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', as Chat stores it.

chat.moderation-request.v1.title: ChatModerationRequest
chat.moderation-request.v1.description: chat.moderation-request@1: what a first-party service hands OpenVibe.Chat's POST /internal/chat/moderation (chat.moderation.write) to change chat rows Chat owns and act on its sockets: delete messages (Chat deletes the rows and broadcasts the delete notices to the room and its mirrors), review messages held for IP approval, hide, unhide or record relay identities, set or clear a TTS voice override, disconnect a person or an address, and log a moderation action. One action per request, applied once per (caller, key): a retry with the same key and body answers the first result, the same key with another body gets 409. The fields an action does not list are refused.

key.description: Idempotency key, scoped to the caller and to this route.

deleted_by.description: The moderator: a user id or a username (chat_messages.deleted_by is text).
The moderator: a user id or a username (chat_messages.deleted_by is text).

oneOf.description: Every visible message of a signed-in person, in one stream or everywhere.

deleted_by.description: The moderator: a user id or a username (chat_messages.deleted_by is text).
The moderator: a user id or a username (chat_messages.deleted_by is text).

oneOf.description: Every visible message stored under a relay username.

from.description: A date Chat parses (Date.parse); compared with the stored message timestamp.

to.description: A date Chat parses (Date.parse); compared with the stored message timestamp.

deleted_by.description: The moderator: a user id or a username (chat_messages.deleted_by is text).

oneOf.description: Every visible message between from and to, in one stream or (without stream_id) in global chat.
By the hidden row's id, or by channel, platform and external username.

params.description: Absent or null: the override is cleared.

oneOf.description: Chat refreshes its ban cache and closes the matching sockets (in one stream, or everywhere).

scope_id.description: A string for scope_type room, otherwise an id.

oneOf.description: Append a row to Chat's moderation log.

chat.moderation-result.v1.title: ChatModerationResult
chat.moderation-result.v1.description: chat.moderation-result@1: what POST /internal/chat/moderation (chat.moderation.write) answers. 200 with the ids a delete action removed (empty when nothing matched), or with the rows another action changed and the id it inserted. A refusal is chat.ingress-ack@1's error: 400 a body Chat refuses, 409 a key reused with another body, 503 Chat or its delivery unavailable (retry with the same key).

id.description: The inserted row (a log entry, a hidden relay identity), else null.

chat.play-request.v1.title: ChatPlayRequest
chat.play-request.v1.description: chat.play-request@1 (the Agent Streams plan, S6): one viewer's request for the chat plays desk to build or do something. A request is written with `!do <request>` (at most 200 characters) in an agent stream's room, `agent:<ags_id>`. One open request per person at a time, and an account younger than a day cannot ask. The request passes the house text filters and the safety check before it is listed; a refused request carries a one-line reason and never enters the queue. Viewers vote with a thumbs-up or `!vote <n>`, and every five minutes, or when the current request finishes, the top request becomes the next task. The owner or a moderator can skip, remove or pin a request. The result is the run's outcome and the scratch site it left behind.

room.description: The room the request was made in: an agent stream's room, `agent:<ags_id>`.

author.description: Who asked. The handle and the display name only, never an id.

handle.description: The handle of the person who asked.

display_name.description: Their display name, when they have one.

text.description: What the viewer asked for, as they typed it (at most 200 characters).

votes.description: How many votes the request has. The count says nothing about who voted.

voters.description: How many people voted (one vote each).

state.description: Where the request stands: queued (waiting), running (the desk is on it), done or failed (it ran), skipped (a moderator or the owner passed over it), removed (it left the queue) or refused (the safety check or the filters turned it down).

pinned.description: A pinned request stays at the top of the queue until it is removed or it runs.

created_at.description: When the request was asked for.

started_at.description: When the desk began it, or null while it waits.

ended_at.description: When it finished, was skipped or was removed, or null while it stands.

refusal.description: Why the request was refused, when it was: the code and the one-line reason the room saw. Null when the request was accepted.

reason.description: The one-line reason shown in the room.

result.description: How the run ended, once it ran: the outcome and the line the overlay and the voice said.

line.description: The one line the room and the overlay saw, e.g. 'Done: a snake game at the scratch address'.

scratch_url.description: The throwaway scratch site the run left, when it left one.

task_id.description: The Codes task that ran it.

chat.send-request.v1.title: ChatSendRequest
chat.send-request.v1.description: chat.send-request@1: what a sender hands OpenVibe.Chat to post a chat line (chat.message.send). From a browser, a frame on WS /ws/chat of type chat in the room the socket joined (the text is trimmed; empty or longer than 6000 characters is dropped, the channel's own max_message_length is enforced after that; a line starting with ! or / is a command, not a message). From Live's bridge, POST /internal/live/calls: a chat.live_bridge.write batch in which every op that sends a message (a chat or dm frame, db saveChatMessage, deployNotice) also needs chat.message.send; without it that op alone is refused. From a first-party service, POST /internal/chat/messages: one line (or one DM) that Chat stores, broadcasts to the room (with mirror, also to global chat and the streamer rooms), reads aloud (tts) and answers with the real id; applied once per (caller, key), the same key with another body gets 409.

reply_to_id.description: Id of a visible message in the room this replies to (parseInt; an unknown or deleted parent is ignored).

auto_delete_minutes.description: Delete the line after this many minutes (clamped to Chat's minimum and maximum; ignored where the channel turned viewer auto-delete off).

voiceChannelId.description: The voice channel the sender is in, echoed on the broadcast.

boot.description: Live's boot id; placeholder message ids are mapped per boot.

op.description: A ChatServer method, a bridge-only op, or db (an allow-listed chat-table write named by args[0]).

ref.description: Live's placeholder id for the row this op inserts.

key.description: Idempotency key, scoped to the caller and to this route.

is_global.description: Default: true when there is no stream and no channel.

auto_delete_at.description: When Chat deletes the line (a date Chat parses).

mirror.description: Also send the line to global chat and the streamer rooms.

dm.description: Send a direct message from user_id instead (no room, mirror, tts or frame; 403 if either blocks the other, 404 if either is unknown).

tts.description: Read the line aloud in its room (needs stream_id or channel_user_id).

frame.description: How the broadcast shows the sender.

first_chat_key.description: Whose first chat in the channel this is (user:, anon: or ext:); default from user_id or anon_id.

chat.send-result.v1.title: ChatSendResult
chat.send-result.v1.description: chat.send-result@1: what chat.message.send answers. On WS /ws/chat nothing is acknowledged directly: the stored line is broadcast as a chat frame to the room (the sender included; channel lines also reach the homepage global feed), and a refusal (banned, slow mode, held for IP approval, a channel rule, not saved) is a system or error frame to the sender alone. On POST /internal/live/calls, the batch result: one entry per op, in order, where a message op without chat.message.send is { ok: false, code: capability.denied }. On POST /internal/chat/messages: { ok: true, id } with the room (stream_id, channel_user_id, first_chat) or the DM (conversation_id, to_user_id), or chat.ingress-ack@1's error ({ ok: false, error }).

username.description: Display name, or the anonymous id.

core_username.description: The immutable login handle; null for an anonymous sender.

role.description: The sender's role, anon for an anonymous sender.

is_global.description: true for homepage global chat (no stream, no channel).

message.description: The parent's text, cut to 100 characters.

vip_badge.description: The channel's VIP member badge, when cached; otherwise a chat_vip_badge frame follows.

first_chat.description: Room only, since 1.2.0: true when this is the sender's first message in this channel's stream (Chat's stream_first_chats), so Live can welcome them without reading its own copy; absent on a DM and from an older Chat.

chat.sound-asset-request.v1.title: ChatSoundAssetRequest
chat.sound-asset-request.v1.description: chat.sound-asset-request@1: the body of POST /internal/chat/sounds/asset on OpenVibe.Chat (capability chat.sounds.write): after OpenVibe.Live's asset sync uploaded a channel sound to OpenVibe.Media, the asset is written back onto Chat's channel_sounds row id. Writing the same asset again is a no-op; an unknown id is 404. Answers chat.ingress-ack@1.

chat.sounds-result.v1.title: ChatSoundsResult
chat.sounds-result.v1.description: chat.sounds-result@1: the answer of GET /internal/chat/sounds on OpenVibe.Chat (capability chat.sounds.read). ?channel_owner_id answers { count } (a channel's custom sounds, for Live's channel readiness); ?pending_asset=1 answers { sounds } (rows with no media_asset_id yet, which Live's asset sync uploads to OpenVibe.Media and writes back with POST /internal/chat/sounds/asset). A failure is chat.ingress-ack@1's error.

command.description: The trigger word (no leading '!'), lowercased: the sound's name.

url.description: Where Chat keeps the audio file (its on-disk path).

media_url.description: The file's OpenVibe.Media URL; null until Live's asset sync uploaded it.

media_asset_id.description: The OpenVibe.Media asset id; null until uploaded.

chat.stats-request.v1.title: ChatStatsRequest
chat.stats-request.v1.description: chat.stats-request@1: the body of POST /internal/chat/stats on OpenVibe.Chat (capability chat.stats.read): one count over chat_messages, for the stats OpenVibe.Live shows without reading its own copy of Chat's tables (home and SEO stats, admin dashboard, star of the day, VOD and recap cards, stream analytics, top chatters, AI slogans). kind site counts all of chat; user one person's messages (user_id); stream one stream's messages, chatters and soundboard plays (stream_id); channel-top the top chatters, of one stream (stream_id) or one channel (channel_user_id), or of all chat when neither is given; site-daily one row per UTC day in [since, until), zero-filled, a kind that takes only since and until. since and until bound chat_messages.timestamp, epoch ms, until exclusive. Deleted messages are never counted. Loopback only, service token.

user_id.description: Live user id; required for kind user.

stream_id.description: Live stream id; required for kind stream.

channel_user_id.description: The broadcaster whose channel room it is (chat_messages.channel_user_id).

since.description: Count messages at or after this instant (epoch ms).

until.description: Count messages before this instant (epoch ms).

limit.description: How many top chatters (channel-top); Chat's default is 10.

chat.stats-result.v1.title: ChatStatsResult
chat.stats-result.v1.description: chat.stats-result@1: the answer of POST /internal/chat/stats (chat.stats.read). site, user and stream answer messages (non-deleted chat_messages rows) and chatters (distinct COALESCE(user_id, anon_id, source_platform || username)); stream also answers sounds (soundboard plays); channel-top answers top_chatters, most messages first; the kind site-daily is answered by chat.site-daily-result@1, not here. A failure is chat.ingress-ack@1's error ({ ok: false, error }).

user_id.description: Live user id; null for an anonymous or relayed chatter, counted by name.

display_name.description: From Chat's copy of the user (ctx_users); null when unknown.

chat.ticket-conversation.v1.title: ChatTicketConversation
chat.ticket-conversation.v1.description: chat.ticket-conversation@1: one conversation between an OpenVibe.Help ticket and one calling service, keyed by the ticket id and the service, carrying one posted message. The person side reads and answers it through Chat's person APIs (POST /api/chat/send needs a person's session); a service-side author (Help's agent worker, staff tooling) posts here with a service token, which is why the write needs the chat.ticket.write capability rather than the person send route. author_kind says who wrote the message (`person`, `agent` or `staff`), author is that author's subject, body is the text, and created_at is when the message was written.
chat.ticket-conversation.v1.$comment: Additive optional fields may extend this v1 contract.

ticket_id.description: The OpenVibe.Help ticket this conversation belongs to. Together with `service` it keys the conversation: one conversation per (ticket id, calling service).

service.description: The Contracts manifest id of the calling service (e.g. `help`, `ai`), the service token's principal. Together with `ticket_id` it keys the conversation, so two services on one ticket get two conversations.

author_kind.description: Who wrote the message: the ticket's `person`, an `agent` (a service acting for one, e.g. Help's AI worker), or `staff` (a human on the service's team).

author.description: The author's subject: `user:<id>` for a person, or the service/agent subject that posted on its behalf. Never a display name.

created_at.description: When the message was written (the author's clock; Chat keeps its own ordering).

message.author: user:usr_01JAB2C3D4E5F6G7H8J9K0MNPQ
message.body: My export from yesterday is missing the last day of records.

chat.timeline-result.v1.title: ChatTimelineResult
chat.timeline-result.v1.description: chat.timeline-result@1: the answer of GET /internal/chat/timeline on OpenVibe.Chat (capability chat.analysis.read): non-deleted chat_messages of one channel (channel_user_id) or stream (stream_id) counted per bucket between since and until (epoch ms), bucket_ms wide, for OpenVibe.Live's AI moments, chat spikes and activity. Live's own AI viewers (source_platform ai) are not counted: they are not people reacting. Empty buckets are left out; buckets are oldest first. max_id is the highest message id in the window, null when none. A failure is chat.ingress-ack@1's error.

people.description: How many different chatters wrote in the bucket (a signed-in user, an anonymous viewer or a relayed name each count once). Optional: Chat from 2026-11-03 sends it; a reader treats its absence as unknown.

chat.tts-speak-request.v1.title: ChatTTSSpeakRequest
chat.tts-speak-request.v1.description: chat.tts-speak-request@1: the body of POST /api/agent-voice/speak (Agent Streams S4). The desk asks Chat for the sound of one line the agent said. TEXT is the line (at most 220 characters). VOICE is a Chat voice id, or absent for the site default. OWN asks for the person own voice, and only the person themself may ask for it.

chat.tts-speak-result.v1.title: ChatTTSSpeakResult
chat.tts-speak-result.v1.description: chat.tts-speak-result@1: the answer of POST /api/agent-voice/speak (Agent Streams S4). AUDIO is the sound of the line (base64), MIME_TYPE what it is, and RATE the sample rate the desk decodes it to (the stream track is 48 kHz).

chat.vibe-ask-request.v1.title: ChatVibeAskRequest
chat.vibe-ask-request.v1.description: chat.vibe-ask-request@1: a first-party service asks Vibe, OpenVibe's assistant, on a person's behalf (Vibe by voice: OpenVibe.Bot passes what the person said after their machine's call word). Chat keeps it in the person's own Vibe chats, one chat per source ("Voice on <machine>"), and answers with Vibe's reply, which counts against the person's daily allowance like any of their Vibe answers. POST /internal/chat/vibe/ask, capability chat.vibe.ask, loopback only.

subject.description: The person Vibe answers, as the calling service vouches (Bot: the machine's owner, with voice on for that machine).

id.description: The source's stable id (the machine's device id): one chat per source.

name.description: What to call it in the chat's name (the machine's name).

idempotency_key.description: The caller's id for this ask (Bot: device id and the voice_ask id): asked again, the same answer, once.

chat.vibe-ask-result.v1.title: ChatVibeAskResult
chat.vibe-ask-result.v1.description: chat.vibe-ask-result@1: Vibe's answer to a chat.vibe-ask-request@1. `answered` carries the reply (plain text, Markdown stripped, for speech); `refused` says why nothing was asked (Vibe resting, the person's daily allowance spent). `url` is the Vibe chat that keeps the question and the answer.

chat.vibe-deliver-request.v1.title: ChatVibeDeliverRequest
chat.vibe-deliver-request.v1.description: chat.vibe-deliver-request@1: a first-party service puts a result of the person's own work into their Vibe chats (OpenVibe.Actor: each finished run of one of their OpenVibe Agents, when the agent sends its results to Vibe). Chat keeps one chat per source, named after it, and posts the text there as Vibe's message, so each run is a chat they can open and continue. No AI answer is made and nothing counts against their allowance. POST /internal/chat/vibe/deliver, capability chat.vibe.deliver, loopback only.

subject.description: The person whose work it is, as the calling service vouches (Actor: the agent's owner).

id.description: The source's stable id (the agent's agt_ id): one chat per source.

name.description: What to call it in the chat's name (the agent's name).

text.description: The result, in Markdown (as Vibe's answers are shown).

url.description: Where the whole run is (its steps, sources and cost).

idempotency_key.description: The caller's id for this result (Actor: the run's task id): sent again, it is posted once.

chat.vibe-deliver-result.v1.title: ChatVibeDeliverResult
chat.vibe-deliver-result.v1.description: chat.vibe-deliver-result@1: where a chat.vibe-deliver-request@1 was posted. `repeated` is true when the idempotency key was seen before (nothing was posted again).

common.config-change.v1.title: ConfigChange
common.config-change.v1.description: common.config-change@1 (AI Exchange D11): body of POST /internal/config/:namespace on a service's openvibe-shared/config admin routes. It proposes a new revision of the namespace and activates it (the store validates against the namespace schema, applies env pins and calls onActivate). `merge: true` starts from the active values; otherwise `values` is the whole new set. `unset` removes keys. A secret-class key's value is never sent here: it is 422 config.secret_write_only; use common.config-secret-put@1.

values.description: The new values, one member per key. The store validates them against the namespace schema; a secret-class value here is refused.

additionalProperties.description: Any JSON value; a redaction marker keeps the value it stands for.

reason.description: Why the change is made; it is the revision's reason in the history.

merge.description: Merge into the active values instead of replacing them.

unset.description: Keys to remove from the new revision.

common.config-namespace.v1.title: ConfigNamespace
common.config-namespace.v1.description: common.config-namespace@1 (AI Exchange D11): one service configuration namespace as openvibe-shared/config's summary() returns it (config-pg.js), plus `sealed`, `pins` and `schema`. GET /internal/config lists these for a service and GET /internal/config/:namespace returns one. Values are the active ones over the defaults, with every secret-class value replaced by its marker; a marker never carries the value. `sealed` says whether the service has a KEK so secrets are envelopes (false is the pre-D11 plaintext behaviour). `pins` names the keys whose x-env variable is set, so their effective value is the environment's and a write is 409 config.pinned_in_env. `schema` is the namespace's JSON Schema so a client can draw the form; its annotations are title, description, x-group, x-env, x-danger, x-bind and x-unit (nano_usd, ms, bps, seconds), and for the owner's Setup tab and the clear admin panel (openvibe-shared 4.125.0) x-owner-input ({ group, unlocks, get_it_at, get_it_how, test }: a field only the owner can give), x-required-for (the feature an unset field blocks), x-enum-labels ({ value: { label, description } }), x-advanced (folded under Advanced settings) and x-example (a placeholder; never on a secret).

revision.description: The active revision; null before the namespace has one.

values.description: The active values over the defaults, one member per key. A secret-class key's value is a marker, never the value.

additionalProperties.description: Any JSON value. An object with a redacted member is a secret marker, and nothing else.

classification.description: Every key of values, classified. A key the service does not classify is internal.

sealed.description: True when the service has a KEK: secret-class values are stored as envelopes and only opened for a caller that needs them. False keeps the pre-D11 plaintext-inside-values_json behaviour, and the tab shows it in red.

pins.description: The keys whose x-env variable is set in the service process: their effective value is the environment's, read-only, and a write answers 409 config.pinned_in_env.

schema.description: The namespace's JSON Schema, or null when it has none. Annotations the client may read: title, description, x-group, x-env, x-danger, x-bind (the key whose value the secret is bound to), x-unit (nano_usd, ms, bps or seconds), x-owner-input, x-required-for, x-enum-labels, x-advanced and x-example.

active.description: The active revision as a snapshot (common.config-snapshot@1), or null.

last_known_good.description: The last revision that activated cleanly (common.config-snapshot@1), or null.

marker.description: A secret-class value, as the summary and the secret endpoints show it: never the value. The fingerprint is keyed, so equal fingerprints within one namespace mean the value did not change.

fingerprint.description: HMAC-SHA256 (hex) of the canonical JSON of the value, keyed with the namespace's secret key.

hint.description: The four-character hint (the value's last four characters), never more.

bound_to.description: The value of the key named by x-bind when the secret was set, e.g. a provider base_url origin.

common.config-snapshot.v1.title: ConfigSnapshot
common.config-snapshot.v1.description: One immutable revision of one service's configuration namespace (roadmap WS-C task 7; kept by openvibe-shared/config). A revision's values never change: revisions grow by one per namespace, and a rollback is a new revision that copies an older one's values. Only the state moves: proposed -> active -> superseded or rolled_back, or proposed -> rejected when validation or activation fails, in which case the previous active revision stays or is restored. A secret-class key's value never appears here: it is { redacted: true, fingerprint }, an HMAC-SHA256 of the value under a secret key the service keeps per namespace, so equal fingerprints within one namespace mean the value did not change, while the value cannot be recovered or guessed offline without that key. checksum is the sha256 of the canonical JSON (keys sorted, no whitespace) of values exactly as they appear here, secrets as their markers, so anyone can check it, and two snapshots of one namespace with the same checksum hold the same configuration.

previous_revision.description: The revision that was active when this one was proposed; null for the namespace's first.

values.description: The configuration, one member per key. A secret-class key's value is a redaction marker.

additionalProperties.description: Any JSON value. An object with a redacted member is a redaction marker, and nothing else.

fingerprint.description: HMAC-SHA256 (hex) of the canonical JSON of the value, keyed with the namespace's secret key: equal within one namespace when the value is unchanged, and not recoverable or guessable without the key.

classification.description: Every key of values, classified. A key the service does not classify is internal.

checksum.description: sha256 (hex) of the canonical JSON of values as they appear in this snapshot (secrets as their markers).

activated_at.description: When it became active; null while proposed, and for a rejected revision.

error.description: Why it was rejected: the validation errors, or what activation reported. Never a secret value.

copied_from.description: A rollback's source: the revision whose values this one copies.

common.owned-resource-control-request.v1.title: OwnedResourceControlRequest
common.owned-resource-control-request.v1.description: common.owned-resource-control-request@1 (ADR-048 amendment 2026-10-15, step 8 phase 2): one control operation on a person-owned resource. Robots, chat rooms, restream definitions and pastes belong to a person, not to a project, so they carry no OVRN and the project-scoped common.resource-control-request@1 cannot name them. OpenVibe.Services sends this to the owning authority's POST /api/v1/resources/control (the same route, told apart by `owned`), acting for the person in on_behalf_of. owned names the resource by its index summary's kind and id. owner is the person it belongs to: the authority refuses unless its own record says the same (Services also offers actions only on the viewer's own resources). A sensitive action (deleting, physical control) asked by an agent is refused with confirmation_required until the owner approves, as for project resources. idempotency_key makes a retry safe: the authority answers a repeated key from the same caller with the first result, and refuses the key reused with another request. Answered with common.resource-control-result@1 (without resource: there is no OVRN). The actions each authority takes are in its <service>.resource.control capability; any other action is refused unsupported.

owned.description: The resource, as its owning authority's resource index lists it (common.resource-summary@1 kind and id).

id.description: The summary's id: a prefixed ULID (rob_…) or the service's own slug (a paste, a room).

owner.description: The person the resource belongs to. Person-owned resources belong to people, never to agents or apps.

params.description: Action-specific input, shaped by the authority's own contract (never redefined here).

on_behalf_of.description: Who asks: the owner, or their agent (whose sensitive actions wait for the owner's approval).

confirmation_id.description: The approved confirmation from an earlier confirmation_required answer.

common.resource-control-result.v1.title: ResourceControlResult
common.resource-control-result.v1.description: common.resource-control-result@1: the authority's answer to a common.resource-control-request@1 (ADR-048, plan T13). state is the outcome, not the resource's own state: done (applied), pending (accepted and asynchronous; the authority reports completion later on its events), refused (a policy or confirmation gate said no) or failed (an error). State rules: refused carries problem or confirmation_required; failed carries problem; done and pending carry neither; confirmation_required appears only on refused. result carries the authority's own response document and never another service's rows. The state rules are checked by contracts.resources.checkControlResult.

confirmation_required.description: The action needs its owner's approval; retry the same request with this confirmation_id once approved.

problem.description: RFC 9457 body when refused or failed.

common.resource-list-result.v1.title: ResourceListResult
common.resource-list-result.v1.description: A page of the resource index (roadmap WS-Z7).

partial.description: Authorities a merged index (OpenVibe.Services, ADR-048) could not read for this page: a slow or failing authority is omitted, never fails the page. Each entry names the authority and the problem code it answered. Added in 1.1.0; a single authority's own index leaves it out.

common.resource-name.v1.title: ResourceName
common.resource-name.v1.description: common.resource-name@1: the one stable, cross-service name of an OpenVibe resource (OVRN; ADR-034 section 2, ADR-048, plan T13): ovrn:<service>:<project_id>:<type>/<id>, for example ovrn:media:prj_01J0000000000000000000000A:object/med_01K0000000000000000000000B. The service segment is the authority that owns the resource; the project segment is its tenancy boundary; type is the second half of a common.resource-summary@1 kind and id is that summary's id, so the name composes from any resource summary. It is used in grant scopes, audit rows, event subjects, usage records, bill lines and console URLs. It never names a person, an app, a request, a session or an event. The pattern is the one common.usage-recorded@1 resource and common.resource-summary@1 ovrn already use.

common.resource-summary.v1.title: ResourceSummary
common.resource-summary.v1.description: One resource of any service, as the resource index lists it (roadmap WS-Z7): every service answers GET /api/v1/resources with these, so OpenVibe.Services shows any resource without owning its data.

kind.description: service.kind, e.g. watch.watch, actor.actor, media.object, events.subscription

ovrn.description: Optional resource name (ADR-034 section 2), the name grants, audit, events, usage records and bills use: ovrn:<service>:<project_id>:<type>/<id>, e.g. ovrn:watch:<project_id>:watch/<wch_id>, with the pattern of common.usage-recorded@1 resource. Its service, project and id are this summary's service, project_id and id. Added in 1.1.0.

errors.problem.v1.title: Problem
errors.problem.v1.description: RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) with a stable OpenVibe error code and trace identifiers. The legacy 'error' string is allowed during migration so existing clients keep working.

error.description: Deprecated compatibility field: same text as title/detail for clients that read {error}.

identity.subject-ref.v1.title: SubjectRef
identity.subject-ref.v1.description: The one cross-platform reference to an actor. Issued by OpenVibe.Network. Never a service-local integer id.

oneOf.description: AgentSubject: an agent (OpenVibe.Actor, or a developer app's agent) acting under grants its owner delegated (roadmap WS-Z2). In an event envelope, on_behalf_of names the owner.

openvibeToken.description: An OpenVibe Network token for this service: a person's token, an app token (client credentials, audience of the service) or a first-party service token. Its `cap` claim must include the capability the operation names.
